We present a system for adapting multimedia Web content to client capabilities.

we present a content adaptation system for multimedia Web documents, that we use a generalized rate-distortion framework to model the selection problem, and that we extend this framework to address multiple resource types at client devices and to allow prioritization among the content items of a Web document.

we have developed a content representation scheme that is suitable for multimedia content and a customizer that selects an optimal content representation based on the client capabilities while providing the most value to the user.

the development of a framework and algorithms for the adaptation of multimedia content for universal access.
developing techniques for adapting the content of Web documents to the client capabilities while maintaining the value of the original content.
developing techniques to enable the delivery of high value multimedia content to a wide range of client devices over the Internet.

we are able to adapt multimedia content to a wide range of client devices while maintaining the value of the content to the end user.
the work described in this thesis has provided a framework and techniques for content adaptation that can be applied to the general case of multimedia Internet content delivery.
the InfoPyramid is a novel and effective representation for multimedia content, and our customizer is an effective and efficient technique for adapting multimedia content to the client capabilities.

we have developed a system that adaptes multimedia content to the capabilities of a diverse range of client devices while preserving the value of the content to the end user.
